topic: the speed of light from Maxwell
prompt: In free space Maxwell's equations give a wave equation whose speed is v = 1 over the square root of mu-nought epsilon-nought. Evaluating it with mu-nought = 4 pi x 10^-7 and epsilon-nought = 8.85 x 10^-12 gives:

options.text: 2.998 x 10^8 m/s, which is exactly the speed of light

explanation: mu-nought times epsilon-nought = 4 pi x 10^-7 x 8.85 x 10^-12 = 1.113 x 10^-17. Its square root is 3.336 x 10^-9, and one divided by that is 2.998 x 10^8 m/s. This is the result the slides call the moment that shook nineteenth-century physics: two constants measured in laboratory experiments about magnets and static charge, with no light involved at all, combine to give the measured speed of light exactly. Maxwell's own conclusion was that we can scarcely avoid the inference that light consists in transverse undulations of the same medium which is the cause of electric and magnetic phenomena.

why.a: Correct, and the agreement with the measured speed of light is the whole point.
why.b: Wrong. 3.34 x 10^-9 is the square root of the product, the number you still have to invert.
why.c: Wrong. 1.11 x 10^-17 is the product itself, before the square root.
why.d: Wrong. 8.99 x 10^9 is Coulomb's constant k, a different combination of the same constants.
why.e: Wrong by a hundred in the exponent.

topic: magnetic amplitude of an EM wave
prompt: A radio transmitter produces an electromagnetic wave with an electric field amplitude of 0.080 V/m. What is the corresponding magnetic field amplitude?
explanation: In an electromagnetic wave the two fields are locked together by E = cB, so B = E over c = 0.080 / 3.0 x 10^8 = 2.67 x 10^-10 T. The magnetic amplitude always comes out tiny beside the electric one, by a factor of the speed of light, which is why radio work quotes E rather than B.

why.b: Wrong. This MULTIPLIES by c instead of dividing, which is the commonest slip here.
why.c: Wrong by a factor of 100 in the exponent.
why.d: Wrong. That is the electric amplitude repeated, in the wrong unit.
why.e: Wrong. That is the speed of light itself, labelled as a field.

prompt: A laser pointer emits 5.0 mW of power in a beam with cross-sectional area 3.0 x 10^-6 m squared. Calculate the intensity.
explanation: Intensity is power per unit area: I = P over A = 5.0 x 10^-3 / 3.0 x 10^-6 = 1667 W/m squared. The interpretation the slide draws is worth keeping: despite a tiny power of only 5 mW, this beats the roughly 1000 W per square metre of full sunlight, because the energy is concentrated into a very small area. That is why a laser pointer is dangerous to the eye and a 5 mW lamp is not.

why.b: Wrong. This MULTIPLIES the power by the area instead of dividing.
why.c: Wrong by a factor of 1000, from leaving the power in milliwatts.
why.d: Wrong. No route to this from these numbers.
why.e: Wrong. 1000 W/m squared is the intensity of SUNLIGHT, the figure being compared against.

prompt: Continuing the laser problem, the intensity is 1667 W/m squared. Using I = one half epsilon-nought c E-nought squared, find the electric field amplitude.
explanation: Rearrange in symbols first: E-nought = square root of (2I over epsilon-nought c). Top: 2 x 1667 = 3334. Bottom: 8.85 x 10^-12 x 3.00 x 10^8 = 2.655 x 10^-3. Dividing gives 1.256 x 10^6, and its square root is about 1120 V/m. The square root at the end is the step to watch, since E-nought appears SQUARED in the intensity formula.

why.a: Correct. The square root of 3334 divided by 2.655 x 10^-3.
why.b: Wrong by a factor of 1000, a slip in the exponent before the square root.
why.c: Wrong. 3334 is the numerator 2I, not the answer.
why.d: Wrong. 2.655 x 10^-3 is the denominator epsilon-nought c.
why.e: Wrong. This forgets the factor of 2 when rearranging the one half.

prompt: Select the properties of electromagnetic waves the slides list.

options.text: Transverse: E and B oscillate perpendicular to the direction of propagation
In vacuum they all travel at c = 3 x 10^8 m/s
They need no medium, unlike sound
E and B are linked at every point by E = cB
They carry energy, with the flux given by the Poynting vector
They travel faster through a dense medium than through vacuum

explanation: Five properties, and the sixth option is false in a way worth knowing: nothing outruns c, and light in fact SLOWS in a medium such as glass or water. Note also that all electromagnetic waves share the same speed in vacuum, from radio at the long end of the spectrum to gamma rays at the short one, and only their frequency and wavelength differ, tied together by c = f lambda.

why.b: Correct, and it is the same c for every part of the spectrum.
why.c: Correct, and it is the property that distinguishes them from sound.
why.d: Correct, which is what makes B tiny compared with E.
why.e: Correct, and the Poynting vector S = one over mu-nought, times E cross B.
why.f: Wrong. Nothing exceeds c, and a medium slows light rather than speeding it.
